title.en: Singular value decomposition as orthogonal map, scale, orthogonal map

summary: Decompose one matrix into three visible stages, keep reflections visible as legitimate orthogonal factors, and connect the ellipsoid semi-axes to the singular values.
objective: Show how a matrix maps the unit sphere through separately inspectable orthogonal-map, nonnegative-scale and orthogonal-map stages, identifying rotations and reflections.
intent_signals: Show what the singular values of a matrix mean geometrically.
Break a linear map into orthogonal maps and nonnegative scaling, including reflections when required.
example_prompts: Build an SVD demonstration where the unit sphere becomes an ellipsoid through three inspectable stages.
Show what happens to the ellipsoid when a singular value goes to zero.
negative_signals: Not a numerical linear algebra tutorial on algorithms or conditioning.
Not a data-analysis or dimensionality-reduction recipe; that mapping needs its own claims.
not_for: Not a numerical linear algebra tutorial on algorithms or conditioning.
Not a data-analysis or dimensionality-reduction recipe; that mapping needs its own claims.

entities.name: Unit sphere and frame
entities.guidance: Draw the sphere with a marked orthonormal frame so an orthogonal map, including a reflection, is visible; a bare sphere makes the first stage invisible.

entities.name: Stage sequence
entities.guidance: Represent the three factors as separate stages with their own progress control, so the composite is never the only thing shown.

entities.name: Ellipsoid axes
entities.guidance: Draw the resulting semi-axes with lengths labelled by singular value and ordered consistently.

state_contract.model: A real 3 by 3 matrix factored as A = U Sigma V^T with U and V orthogonal (determinant plus or minus one) and Sigma diagonal with nonnegative entries in descending order. Stages are applied to column vectors in the order V^T, then Sigma, then U, and the reported determinant sign of each orthogonal factor states whether it is a rotation or includes a reflection.
state_contract.authority: The factorisation is authoritative; the sphere, ellipsoid and axes are all rendered from the current stage parameter applied to that factorisation.
actions: Drive a singular value to zero and inspect the collapse.
Reset the matrix and the stage parameter.

invariants: Semi-axis lengths equal the singular values in the declared order; a relabelled axis is a defect.

The two orthogonal stages preserve the lengths and angles they receive: applied to the unit sphere V^T keeps it a unit sphere, while U applied after Sigma preserves the already-scaled ellipsoid rather than restoring unit lengths.
Rank is reported and drawn honestly: rank 3 gives an ellipsoid, rank 2 a filled elliptical disc, rank 1 a segment and rank 0 a single point at the origin.
Singular values are never negative; a sign that belongs to the mapping is carried by the orthogonal factors, whose determinants are reported as plus or minus one.
motion_guidance: Animate one stage at a time. A factor with determinant minus one cannot be reached from the identity through orthogonal matrices, so any smooth in-between frames for that stage are presentation and must be labelled as an interpolation rather than as intermediate orthogonal maps.
Keep the frame markers attached through the whole sequence so the correspondence between input and output directions is traceable.
known_limits: Sign and ordering conventions differ between libraries, so the scene states its stage order (V^T, Sigma, U) and its column-vector convention. Calling the outer stages rotations is wrong whenever a factor has determinant minus one, for example with A = diag(-1, 2, 3).
The demonstration uses small matrices; nothing here addresses numerical stability at scale.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The singular value decomposition writes any matrix A as a product U Sigma V transpose, where U and V are orthogonal and Sigma is diagonal, and the columns of U and V give bases for the four fundamental subspaces.
claims.scope: Real matrices with orthogonal factors, which include reflections as well as rotations; the cited overview asserts orthogonality and diagonality, not that either factor is a proper rotation.

claims.statement: A documented implementation returns u and vh with orthonormal columns and rows and returns the singular values sorted in descending order.
claims.scope: Contract of one library version; ordering and shape conventions must be checked against whatever library the scene uses.

object_craft.structure: A sphere with latitude and longitude bands plus three orthonormal axis markers rooted at the origin.
object_craft.material: Matte translucent shell so the interior frame stays visible; bands are geometry, not a texture, so they deform correctly.
object_craft.articulation: The shell is transformed by the current stage, never re-authored per stage.

object_craft.structure: Three semi-axis rods with end caps and numeric labels placed outside the surface.
object_craft.material: One accent per axis with distinct value steps so the ordering is readable in monochrome.
object_craft.articulation: Rebuilt from the factorisation whenever the matrix changes.

physical_contract.scope: Mathematical transformation of authored geometry; no physical deformation is implied.
checks: Applying all three stages equals applying the original matrix directly.
Setting a singular value to zero reports a rank drop.
Each orthogonal factor reports its determinant, and a reflection is presented as a reflection rather than animated as a rotation.
